english.title: Commander / owner of aircraft flown in contravention of instruction made by an officer / constable
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) were the

(A)_[commander]_
(B)_[owner]_

of an aircraft, namely **(..SPECIFY THE AIRCRAFT..), flown in contravention of instructions given by

(C)_[an officer,]_
(D)_[a constable,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE OFFICER OR CONSTABLE..), to whom it appeared that an aircraft had intended, or had been likely, to depart for a destination outside the United Kingdom and the Isle of Man from a

(E)_[place other than a customs and excise airport]_
(F)_[customs and excise airport before clearance was given]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 34(3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
commander / owner of an aircraft
flown in contravention of instructions
given by an officer / PC
to whom it appears that
an aircraft is intended / likely to depart
for a destination outside the UK / Isle of Man
from a place other than
a customs and excise airport OR
a customs and excise airport
before clearance is given

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 34(3) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979 provides that it is a defence to prove that the flight took place without the defendant's consent or connivance.
